The 5G NAS security context is a security state maintained by both the User Equipment (UE) and the Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) to enable secure exchange of Non-Access Stratum (NAS) signaling messages in 5G networks. It encompasses critical security parameters, including integrity protection, ciphering, NAS COUNT values (both uplink and downlink), message authentication codes, selected NAS algorithms, and a key set identifier (ngKSI). The context is established during primary authentication and key agreement, security mode control procedures, N1-to-N1 handovers, or inter-system transitions from S1 mode to N1 mode. It supports both 3GPP and non-3GPP access within the same PLMN, maintaining separate NAS COUNT counters for each access type—resulting in two pairs of counters when both access types are used. The context may be native (independent of prior contexts) or mapped (derived from a previous context, e.g., during handover), and is activated upon successful registration with the same PLMN over either 3GPP or non-3GPP access. The current 5G NAS security context refers to the most recently established and active instance, while non-current contexts are retained temporarily to ensure continuity<SEP>A 5G NAS security context is a set of security parameters maintained by the AMF and UE to enable secure exchange of NAS messages. 5G Multicast-Broadcast Service (MBS) is a service designed to provide efficient downlink delivery of user traffic for mission critical (MC) group communications. MBS sessions are established to deliver user data in downlink to multiple MC users, either through point-to-point or point-to-multipoint transmission over the radio. The service area for broadcast or local MBS sessions is configured via the MBS session. MBS enhances reliability and minimizes data loss due to mobility and handover.
